lesson.title: Article Gym: 20 Nouns, 3 Colors
lesson.subtitle: Rapid der/die/das assignment with every table noun you have met

hook.title: The Color Reflex
hook.content: Twenty nouns you already own. One job: attach the right flag — der (blue), die (rose), das (green) — without hesitating. This gym is not about logic; it is about reps. Every noun below has already met you in a lesson, carrying its flag. Today you prove the flags stuck. Speed round, three colors, twenty nouns — and every miss feeds the retry queue until the reflex is permanent.

footnotes.title: Why the App Uses Colors
footnotes.content: der = blue, die = rose, das = green across every table, drawer, and card in Brücke. Gender is ancestry, not logic — so it is learned like pronunciation: by exposure and repetition, one color at a time.

pattern.title: The Noun Lineup
pattern.content: das Haus, das Glas, das Brot, das Gold — the neuter home-and-matter set. der Kaffee, der Tee, der Tisch, der Traum, der Tag, der Sand — the masculine café-and-time set. die Butter, die Zeit, die Milch, die Straße, die Tochter — the feminine flow set. das Wasser, das Buch — two exceptions to enjoy. Spot the soft patterns when they appear (many -e nouns are die; German drinks are der) but trust the colors first — heuristics get their own lesson later.
pattern.linguist_note: A quiet head start: agent nouns ending in -er are always der (der Fernseher, der Staubsauger), and -chen/-lein are always das — two laws you will formalize in the Gender Heuristics lesson.

exercises.explanation: das Haus — the neuter flag, green in the app's colors.
die Zeit — and most -e nouns share the rose flag, though the proof is always the word itself.

exercises.prompt: Match each noun with its article:
exercises.target_answer: der Kaffee, die Butter, das Glas, die Straße
exercises.meaning: the coffee, the butter, the glass, the street
exercises.explanation: Café drinks lean masculine; das Glas keeps its neuter flag from the Hidden Twins lesson.

exercises.prompt: Complete the Determiner × Case matrix for the masculine accusative ('a'):
exercises.column_law: Column: Nominative subject vs. Accusative object
exercises.explanation: ein marches in step with der: in the accusative Him-Case, der → den and ein → einen (kurz gesagt). [Ref: der Kaffee, die Zeit, das Wasser]

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'The time is short' (with the article)
exercises.meaning: Die Zeit ist kurz = The time is short

vocab_hints.note: no English twin needed — it survives in the name Kurt

exercises.explanation: die Zeit with its rose flag, capitalized mid-sentence like every German noun.

summary.outcome: Assign der/die/das to twenty high-frequency nouns without hesitation.
summary.takeaway: Gender is collected with the word, flagged in color — reps build the reflex before rules explain it.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next: jener ↔ yon — the far demonstrative, and the full map of this/that/yon in one grid.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — rebuild the core sentence from Article Gym: 20 Nouns, 3 Colors (Die Zeit ist kurz = The time is short):
twist.explanation: Re-assembling "Die Zeit ist kurz" from scratch locks in the structural pattern of Article Gym: 20 Nouns, 3 Colors without relying on short-term echo.

die.etymology_derivation: th → d. Sounds identical to emphatic English "thee".

das.shift_rule: TH → D + T → S / SS / Z
das.etymology_derivation: Double shift: th → d and final t → s.

haus.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hūsą — an exact twin of English house, down to the diphthong. [wiktionary]

brot.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *braudą — originally "the fermented/risen thing", kin to the verb brew (German brauen). Bread is "the brewed thing". [wiktionary]

gold.context_phrase: Nicht alles, was glänzt, ist Gold.
gold.context_translation: Not all that glitters is gold.

sand.context_translation: The children play in the sand.

butter.etymology_derivation: Borrowed together into West Germanic from Latin butyrum / Greek boutyron.

tisch.context_phrase: Der Teller steht auf dem Tisch.
tisch.context_translation: The plate stands on the table.
tisch.etymology_derivation: Latin discus → Old English disc (dish/desk) → Old High German tisc (tisch, with d → t).

tag.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and y → g.

zeit.etymology_derivation: t → z [ts] (cognate with English "tide", as in Yuletide or time and tide).

buch.context_translation: I am reading a good book.

straße.etymology_derivation: Roman paved road (via strata) gave English "street" (kept Latin "t") and German "Straße" (shifted "t" to sharp "ß").

tochter.context_phrase: Meine Tochter lernt in der Schule.
tochter.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and gh → ch.
